_meta.description: Audibility threshold rules for fire alarm notification appliances. Thresholds are RELATIVE (computed against a measured ambient sound level), not fixed dB targets. The audibility calculator must take a measured ambient reading as input, not assume one.
notes: publicMode and privateMode both use a 'greater of two rules' comparison: (ambient average + offset) vs (60-second max ambient + fixedOffsetDb). The calculator's Result should surface WHICH rule governed, not just the final number — useful for the pass/fail explanation.

sleepingArea threshold is an absolute floor (dBA at pillow), not ambient-relative, but the relative public/private rule can still override it upward if the space's ambient is high enough. Both must be checked and the greater taken.

maximumAllowedDba is a hard ceiling across all modes — exists to prevent hearing damage. Any calculated target above this should be flagged as a design conflict (occupancy needs sound suppression/ANC, not a louder horn), not silently capped.

private.notes: Typical use case: healthcare occupancies, staff-alert-only zones.

sleepingArea.lowFrequencyAppliesTo: New installations per 2019+ editions; verify applicability for retrofit/existing systems before enforcing in calculator output.

averageAmbientSoundLevelByOccupancy._action_required: Transcribe from NFPA 72 Table A.18.4.3 (2022 ed.) using your existing PEC-table transcription workflow (image -> Python script -> spot-check). Do not hand-populate from memory or search fragments — this table feeds pass/fail life-safety output and should follow the same verified-source discipline as PEC Table 10.1.1.1.
